title: Claude Code tests, loads and screenshots a Chrome extension to fix its own failed runs
summary: A developer tired of babysitting broken AI-written code had Claude Code run the tests, load the Chrome extension and screenshot the result. Failed runs now get fixed before he looks at them.
agent_role: Claude Code runs the tests, loads the extension in Chrome, checks screenshots and fixes failures on its own. The human wired up the loop and reviews the finished result.
outcome: Author estimates roughly 3 out of 4 of his "why is this broken" moments are gone.
what_they_did: A developer building a Chrome extension wired Claude Code to check its own work. After each change, the agent runs the test suite, loads the extension in Chrome and takes a screenshot of the result. It then fixes any failures before handing the work back.
how_it_went: The author says failed runs he used to babysit now fix themselves before he sees them. He estimates about three in four of his debugging moments have disappeared.
prompt: For every change you make to [project, e.g. my Chrome extension], verify it yourself before reporting back. First run the test suite with [test command]. Then load the extension in Chrome and take a screenshot of [the page or popup to check]. If a test fails or the screenshot looks wrong, fix the problem and repeat. Only report back once tests pass and the screenshot matches what I asked for. Include the final screenshot and a short list of what you fixed. Do not commit or push anything without my approval.

curation.rationale: A genuine self-verification loop where Claude Code runs tests, loads a Chrome extension and screenshots the result. It is very thin, with only a rough self-estimate and no setup details.
